samples.summary: `void runCli()` drops the promise with no `.catch()`, so any throw from the catch-handler path becomes an unhandled rejection
samples.evidence: bin.ts:6 is `void runCli();`. `runCli` only guards `program.parseAsync(...)` (cli.ts:55-59); if `outputError(e)` itself throws inside that catch — e.g. `console.error` failing with EPIPE when stderr is a closed pipe, or `JSON.stringify` throwing on a thrown value with a circular/throwing `message` getter — the rejection escapes `runCli` and, because the promise is `void`ed rather than `.catch()`ed, Node reports an unhandled rejection and exits with a stack trace instead of the documented `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope. The whole point of the change is that the entrypoint always produces the envelope; the last hop is unguarded.

samples.summary: Progress notice is written to stdout (console.log), contradicting the new `--quiet` contract the change documents
samples.evidence: root.ts:55-57 now documents `--quiet` as "Suppress progress notices (result body and errors still print)", and formatter.ts:21-24 states the body is the thing callers redirect on stdout. But `sheets export <file>` emits its progress notice with `console.log('Exported to ${file}')` on **stdout** (sheets-export.ts:52-53), not stderr like every other notice (`io.stderr` in docs/content.ts:142, binary.ts:39, slides/content.ts:105). With the new semantics a caller doing `wafflebase sheets export doc f.csv > log` gets a human sentence on the stream that is now defined to carry only machine-readable body output. Pre-existing site, but the change is what fixes the stream contract everywhere else and leaves this one inconsistent.

samples.summary: `sheets cells batch --dry-run` still blocks on stdin before the dry-run short-circuit when `--data` is omitted
samples.evidence: The refactor moved the dry-run check (cells.ts:128-136) inside the try but kept it *after* the stdin drain at cells.ts:121-125. Without `--data` and without a pipe (interactive TTY), `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` never completes, so `--dry-run` hangs instead of printing the planned request. Unlike `docs import`/`notes import`, which special-case dry-run against the confirmation/TTY gate (docs/import.ts:121-124), there is no TTY guard here. Behavior is unchanged by the diff, but the diff is what reorganized this block.
